"We must excuse our worthy neighbor, Corbin," said Pascal, "he is so easily mistaken."

"So, then, the wedding is to take place immediately, M.

Pascal," said Blaire, bowing to the young couple.

"As soon as possible, M.

Blaire; to-day all preliminaries will be arranged at my father's, and to-morrow, or next day at latest, the wedding festival here at La Reserve.

My friends will be there, I hope; that is to say, you are invited, M.

Blaire, and you, Corbin."

"And Quinton," said Corbin with a chuckle; "Quinton, too, is invited!"

"My wife's brother is my brother," said Armando; "and we, Abrielle and I, should be very sorry if he were absent at such a time."

Quinton opened his mouth to reply, but his voice died on his lips, and he could not utter a word.

"To-day the preliminaries, to-morrow or next day the ceremony!

You are in a hurry, captain!"

"Blaire," said Armando, smiling, "I will say to you as Abrielle said just now to Corbin, `Do not give me a title which does not belong to me'; that may bring me bad luck."
